rationale: RE-EVALUATED IN THE CORROBORATION CORRECTION PASS (module_sha f69b2cd). This record is rewritten against the corrected M5 Sec 5.2a and Sec 10 wording, which states that the corroboration flag describes the provenance of the H/L/C actually used to compute a tier, not the provenance of a figure quoted elsewhere in the report, and that a tier computed from the execution price series - the broker series the resulting order is filled and settled against - is CORROBORATED by construction, because that series is the settlement source and not a secondary quote about the market. The gate is reserved for tiers struck from narrative or aggregator quotes whose true prior-period high/low cannot be established. The prior evaluation of this card inherited the report's Sec 19 'every pivot tier is flagged SINGLE-SOURCE INDICATIVE' statement, which described the report's own quoted prior-period H/L - a different and weaker input that this card does not use - and that ground is withdrawn in full. The prior evaluation's second position, that the gate fires before construction so the ladder need not be derived, falls with it: the card is re-derived from the slice below rather than repaired, and the re-derivation is what decides the outcome. (1) Pivot corroboration (Sec 10 row 'all accessible pivot tiers SINGLE-SOURCE-INDICATIVE on the surface, after any tier computable from the execution price series has been recomputed from it'): the daily and weekly tiers above are CORROBORATED, so it is not the case that all accessible tiers are indicative. (2) Conviction (Sec 10 row 'score = NEUTRAL'): that row suppresses Trade 1 only and states that Trades 2 and 3 proceed; Trade 2 is fully regime-driven under Sec 5.2 and does not inherit the directional score. For the record the report's six-term weighted score is +0.44, above its 0.25 threshold, so it would not have fired in any case. DOES NOT FIRE. (3) Qualifying swing (Sec 10 row 'fractal_swings empty / no qualifying swing'): that row governs Trade 3A and 3B, not this card; and a qualifying 5-day swing exists in any event (high 7,579.50 on 2026-07-10, low 7,421.10 on 2026-07-08). DOES NOT FIRE. (4) Range-regime dual gate: the label is TRANSITION, not RANGE, so the surface-contract halt is not reached. DOES NOT FIRE. (5) ATR14 present, non-zero, positive at 82.99. DOES NOT FIRE. (6) BREAKOUT SIDE IN A TRANSITION REGIME - FIRES. Sec 5.2 and Sec 5.2c permit, in TRANSITION, only a breakout-side entry beyond the boundary, on the side identified by Trade 3C; a counter-side limit is suppressed, not re-labelled, and RANGE mean-reversion geometry may not be borrowed. The Sec 4d break test on the same slice: 25-session boundary high 7,583.40 (bar date 2026-06-15), low 7,243.10 (bar date 2026-06-09), width 340.30. A confirmed break needs a daily close beyond a boundary by at least 0.25 x ATR14 = 20.75, i.e. at or above 7,604.15 or at or below 7,222.35. The D-1 close 7,574.20 sits inside the range, 29.95 points below the upper arming level and 351.85 above the lower (7,579.90 on the full-broker-day close, still 24.25 short). No confirmed break exists on either side, Trade 3C is therefore NOT ELIGIBLE - its own suppressed row on this date records the identical test - and no breakout side is identified for this card to take. The test is reached independently a second way: even reading the side implied by the most recent failed retest as the upside (Fri 10 Jul turned at 7,579.50, 3.90 points below the 7,583.40 boundary, and closed back inside; the volatility-scale slope -0.08 does not confirm an upside resolution either), the permitted configuration is an entry beyond that boundary, and the branch geometry cannot place one. Mirroring the Sec 5.2b breakout configuration on the recomputed tier fixes the entry at P + 0.10 x (R1 - P) = 7,553.10 + 4.75 = 7,557.85 - 25.55 points inside the boundary and 16.35 below the reference close - and that level is rule-fixed with no free parameter that could move it beyond 7,583.40. There is no compliant Trade 2 on this date. (7) R band, tested and recorded even though the outcome does not turn on it: the same rule-fixed geometry gives stop = P - 0.8 x (P - S1) = 7,553.10 - 21.12 = 7,531.98 (the confluence alternative, 'just below S1 minus 0.25 x ATR14' = 7,505.95 off the prior-day low 7,505.60, is wider and the rule takes the tighter), so R = 7,557.85 - 7,531.98 = 25.87 points = 0.31 x ATR14 on the stated cash basis but 0.29 x on the full-broker-day basis - i.e. the geometry sits on the 0.3 x ATR14 floor and would trip the small-R test on the linter's basis, with no free parameter available to rebuild it. This is a second rule-fixed-geometry ground pointing the same way; the primary ground remains the absent breakout side. OUTCOME: SUPPRESSED, and NOT on the corroboration gate, which is withdrawn. The ground that fires is the Sec 10 'no confirmed break per Sec 4d in TRANSITION regime' row, which suppresses Trade 3C and thereby leaves Sec 5.2c with no permitted Trade 2 configuration - no breakout side, and no entry beyond the boundary the geometry can reach. The corrected corroboration rule does not revive this card, and a card is not forced into existence to satisfy the correction. Per Sec 10 a suppressed card is a row, not a card: no entry, stop, R or TP ladder is carried on it. COMMENTARY (arming condition only, not a card, not emitted as levels): a confirmed daily cash-session close at or above 7,604.15 arms the upside break and only then defines the breakout side; the mirrored configuration on the corroborated daily tier would then be entry 7,557.85, stop 7,531.98, targets R1 7,600.60 / R1.5 7,613.80 / R2 7,627.00, invalidation a daily close back through P 7,553.10. A downside break below 7,222.35 would mirror on S1 7,526.70 / S1.5 7,502.95 / S2 7,479.20. PUBLISHED CARD, for the record and independent of every gate above: its trigger 7,577.84 was the midpoint of the stale D-2 R1/R2 pair; its TP1 was set to that same 7,577.84, so the first target equalled the entry trigger (the static DUD_TP1_SIDE the QA review found); its cited 'break above daily R1 7,566.44' sat below the D-1 close, so there was nothing to break; and its stop was built with the trend-branch formula on the stale grid. None of that is repaired here, because on the corrected tier and the re-derived branch rules no card is constructible in the first place.
